notes.note: NASA's caption for this ISS photo (iss068e027781) says it was taken "the day before its Full Moon phase," not before launch. It's dated Dec. 7, 2022, about three weeks after Artemis I launched Nov. 16, 2022, while Orion was already in transit near the Moon.
notes.claim: A photo of the moon was taken from the International Space Station the day before Artemis 2 launched.
notes.context_quote: This photo was taken from the International Space Station the day before Artemis launched specifically to say, "Hey everybody, look, this is where they're going."
notes.context_paragraph: In fact, I want to start with a photo that was taken before the Artemis mission started. This photo was taken from the International Space Station the day before Artemis launched specifically to say, "Hey everybody, look, this is where they're going."

sources.quote: iss068e027781 (Dec. 7, 2022) — The Moon is pictured the day before its Full Moon phase from the International Space Station
sources.explanation: This confirms the image ID, the date it was taken (Dec 7, 2022), and that the 'day before' description refers to the lunar phase, not a launch.

sources.quote: At the time of this photograph the Orion vehicle on the Artemis I mission was 234,100 miles from Earth and 127,700 miles from the Moon
sources.explanation: This confirms the Artemis I mission was already in progress when the photo was taken, contradicting the claim it was taken before launch.
